newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India slides as political woes mount.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India slides as political woes mount.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) came under heavy pressure in London after former prime minister PV Narasimha Rao was charged in a forgery case.
"It was a very meaty day in the market, a lot of selling and with the Bombay index below support at 3,287, the next level is 300 points away," said a trader.

The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed down 2.35 points, 3.51 percent, at 64.67 points, with the premium over the local market at 9.94 percent after the Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index fell 52.32 points, 1.58 percent, to 3,254.73.
"I did not struggle to fulfil any buy orders I had, but struggled to fill sell orders," said a trader.
He noted that there had been some client demand at the very bottom of today's trade, but not very much.
"It was non-aggressive, very selective buying," he said.

Traders believe that if the slide in the domestic market continues, a new order will emerge in the GDRs on London's SEAQ International under which some of the second-line stocks will simply not be traded.
"Some of these stocks are just going to die," said one.

With the Korean and Taiwanese domestic markets closed, there was little business done on the GDRs, with the Capel Korea GDR Index up 0.51 points at 71.02 points, a premium of 31.08 percent, and the Capel Taiwan GDR Index up 0.19 points at 89.48, a premium of 3.04 percent.
